meta_description_en: Neil Currie reviews text adventure games and publishers supporting the Sinclair ZX Spectrum +D disk system, including Quest, Compass, FSF, and Gilsoft.
meta_description_ru: Нил Керри рассказывает о текстовых приключениях для ZX Spectrum, выходящих на дисковой системе +D: релизы от Quest Software, Compass, FSF и новости о PAW.
body_en_plain:
Adventures on the +D
         By Neil Currie
      --------------------

This is an intoduction to some
of the adventures now being
released onto the +D.

The Spectrum is the still best-
supported computer for home-
grown adventures and the authors
are now taking advantage of the
+D for their programs.


I don't need to go into details
about the reliability and
advantages of loading and saving
to disk over tape so will deal
with some of the programs now
available.

The first adventure I will cover
is the "controversial" Doomsday
by Quest Software. There are two
versions of Doomsday on the disk
-one is called the"nasty"version
and has many violent scenes -
while the second is a toned-down
version. These are both 128k
programs but the disk also has a
two-part 48k adventure called
Leotrope plus another called
Cell of the Ridges. It also
contains an early version of the
Alchnews PD tapezine.


This is a good value package for
`4.99 though some of the scenes
are very graphic in the nasty
version. Their address is Quest
Software, 10 Westerkirk Drive,
Maidley, Telford, Shropshire.
TF7 5RJ.


Dragon Slayer is a fantasy
adventure from Dream World
Adventures available in 48k or
128k versions. It is an easier
game than some and its sequel,
Death or Glory, should be
available by the time you read
this. Contact them at Dream
World Adventures, 10 Medhurst
Crescent, Gravesend, Kent, DA12
4HL.


If you bought Your Sinclair No.
82 then you already know the
high standard of Compass advent-
ures. The Anttilis Mission is
just one of a range of advent-
ures from Compass, selling at
`1.99 each.


When Compass first started
providing games on the +D, they
had an offer of five of their
older games on one disk for
`2.50,and you might like to see
if this is still available.


Write to Compass Software, 111
Mill Road, Cobholm Island, Great
Yarmouth,Norfolk. NR31 OBB.


Sinclair User have had many of
FSF Adventures 48k programs on
their covertapes in later
issues. Magnetic Moon and
Starship Quest have been given
away and they are now covering
The Axe of Kolt.


More games are available on disk
from FSF, plus the highly
expanded 128k versions of the
above, and some conversions from
the Amiga to Spectrum.


Their address is FSF Adventures,
40 Harvey Gardens, Charlton,
London. SE7 8AJ.



I wrote to the two main suppli-
ers of adventures asking if they
had any plans to release games
on the +D in the future. Both
The Guild and Zenobi have no
plans to do so - though both do
supply games for the Spectrum+3.
In fact, +3 owners have had the
best for adventures with produc-
ers such as Magnetic Scrolls and
Topologika releasing +3 only
products in the past.

Their addresses are...

The Guild, 760 Tyburn Road,
Erdington, Birmingham. B24 9NX.
              and...
Zenobi Software,26 Spotland,Tops
Cutgate, Rochdale, Lancashire.
OL12 7NX.


Both have a large selection of
adventures by many different
authors. (The Guild even sells
The Golden Cobra by Brian
Cavers!) [with permission!-BC]

Zenobi are in the process of
converting their catalogue of
over 100 games to +3 disk though
in many cases the tape deck is
still used to save and load
"saved" parts of adventures.
Indeed, it is really only PAW
games that work completely on
disk formats.

Gilsoft,who wrote PAW, converted
it to all systems including +D
and +3.Owners of the tape vers-
ion of PAW can upgrade to a +D
version for `4.49 or +3 version
for `5.50.

Alternatively, you can buy it
for `20.95 for both systems.
This allows you to load PAWed
adventures from tape and trans-
fer them onto disk (and also
change the unreadable fonts some
adventures have). Gilsoft can be
contacted at Gilsoft, 2 Park
Crescent, Barry, South Glamorgan
CF6 8HD.

There is a large choice for +D
adventurers, so why don't you
send an SAE to some of them for
their latest prices and releas-
es?

                  - Neil Currie.
body_en:
## Adventures on the +D
**By Neil Currie**

This is an introduction to some of the adventures now being released onto the +D.

The Spectrum is still the best-supported computer for home-grown adventures, and the authors are now taking advantage of the +D for their programs.

I don't need to go into details about the reliability and advantages of loading and saving to disk over tape, so will deal with some of the programs now available.

The first adventure I will cover is the "controversial" *Doomsday* by Quest Software. There are two versions of *Doomsday* on the disk — one is called the "nasty" version and has many violent scenes, while the second is a toned-down version. These are both 128k programs, but the disk also has a two-part 48k adventure called *Leotrope*, plus another called *Cell of the Ridges*. It also contains an early version of the *Alchnews* PD tapezine.

This is a good value package for £4.99, though some of the scenes are very graphic in the nasty version. Their address is:

Quest Software, 10 Westerkirk Drive, Maidley, Telford, Shropshire, TF7 5RJ.

*Dragon Slayer* is a fantasy adventure from Dream World Adventures, available in 48k or 128k versions. It is an easier game than some, and its sequel, *Death or Glory*, should be available by the time you read this. Contact them at:

Dream World Adventures, 10 Medhurst Crescent, Gravesend, Kent, DA12 4HL.

If you bought *Your Sinclair* No. 82, then you already know the high standard of Compass adventures. *The Anttilis Mission* is just one of a range of adventures from Compass, selling at £1.99 each.

When Compass first started providing games on the +D, they had an offer of five of their older games on one disk for £2.50, and you might like to see if this is still available.

Write to:

Compass Software, 111 Mill Road, Cobholm Island, Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, NR31 0BB.

*Sinclair User* have had many of FSF Adventures' 48k programs on their covertapes in recent issues. *Magnetic Moon* and *Starship Quest* have been given away, and they are now covering *The Axe of Kolt*.

More games are available on disk from FSF, plus the highly expanded 128k versions of the above, and some conversions from the Amiga to Spectrum.

Their address is:

FSF Adventures, 40 Harvey Gardens, Charlton, London, SE7 8AJ.

I wrote to the two main suppliers of adventures asking if they had any plans to release games on the +D in the future. Both The Guild and Zenobi have no plans to do so — though both do supply games for the Spectrum +3. In fact, +3 owners have had the best for adventures, with producers such as Magnetic Scrolls and Topologika releasing +3-only products in the past.

Their addresses are:

The Guild, 760 Tyburn Road, Erdington, Birmingham, B24 9NX.

and...

Zenobi Software, 26 Spotland Tops, Cutgate, Rochdale, Lancashire, OL12 7NX.

Both have a large selection of adventures by many different authors. (The Guild even sells *The Golden Cobra* by Brian Cavers!) [with permission! — BC]

Zenobi are in the process of converting their catalogue of over 100 games to +3 disk, though in many cases the tape deck is still used to save and load "saved" parts of adventures. Indeed, it is really only PAW games that work completely on disk formats.

Gilsoft, who wrote PAW, converted it to all systems, including +D and +3. Owners of the tape version of PAW can upgrade to a +D version for £4.49 or a +3 version for £5.50.

Alternatively, you can buy it for £20.95 for both systems. This allows you to load PAWed adventures from tape and transfer them onto disk (and also change the unreadable fonts some adventures have). Gilsoft can be contacted at:

Gilsoft, 2 Park Crescent, Barry, South Glamorgan, CF6 8HD.

There is a large choice for +D adventurers, so why don't you send an SAE to some of them for their latest prices and releases?

— Neil Currie.
body_ru:
## Текстовые приключения на дисковой системе +D
**Нил Керри**

Это краткий обзор некоторых текстовых квестов (adventures), которые сейчас выходят на дисковой системе +D.

ZX Spectrum по-прежнему остается платформой с наилучшей поддержкой для любительских адвенчур, и их авторы теперь активно используют преимущества системы +D.

Думаю, нет нужды расписывать надежность и удобство дисковой загрузки и сохранения по сравнению с кассетами, поэтому сразу перейду к доступным играм.

Первая адвенчура, о которой пойдет речь, — это «скандальная» *Doomsday* от Quest Software. На диске записаны две версии *Doomsday*: одна так называемая «жесткая» (nasty), изобилующая сценами насилия, а вторая — слегка смягченная. Обе рассчитаны на 128k, но на диске также присутствуют двухчастная 48k-игра *Leotrope* и еще одна — *Cell of the Ridges*. Кроме того, туда включен ранний выпуск кассетного PD-журнала *Alchnews*.

За £4.99 это очень выгодное предложение, хотя некоторые сцены в «жесткой» версии весьма откровенны. Адрес разработчиков:

Quest Software, 10 Westerkirk Drive, Maidley, Telford, Shropshire. TF7 5RJ.

*Dragon Slayer* — это фэнтезийное приключение от Dream World Adventures, доступное в версиях для 48k и 128k. Игра несколько проще аналогов, а ее продолжение, *Death or Glory*, должно выйти уже к моменту публикации этой статьи. Написать им можно по адресу:

Dream World Adventures, 10 Medhurst Crescent, Gravesend, Kent, DA12 4HL.

Если вы покупали журнал *Your Sinclair* № 82, то уже знаете о высоком уровне игр от Compass. *The Anttilis Mission* — лишь одна из целой линейки приключений этой студии, которые продаются по £1.99 за штуку.

Когда Compass только начинали выпускать игры на +D, они предлагали комплект из пяти старых игр на одном диске всего за £2.50. Возможно, это предложение действует и сейчас.

Пишите:

Compass Software, 111 Mill Road, Cobholm Island, Great Yarmouth, Norfolk. NR31 OBB.

Журнал *Sinclair User* в последних номерах часто размещал 48k-игры от FSF Adventures на своих приложениях к журналу. Среди них были *Magnetic Moon* и *Starship Quest*, а сейчас они обозревают *The Axe of Kolt*.

У FSF на дисках доступно еще больше игр, включая значительно расширенные 128k-версии упомянутых проектов, а также конверсии с Amiga на Spectrum.

Их адрес:

FSF Adventures, 40 Harvey Gardens, Charlton, London. SE7 8AJ.

Я написал двум крупнейшим поставщикам приключенческих игр с вопросом, планируют ли они выпускать свои проекты на +D в будущем. И The Guild, и Zenobi ответили отрицательно — хотя обе компании поставляют игры для Spectrum +3. На самом деле, владельцам +3 в плане адвенчур повезло больше всех: такие разработчики, как Magnetic Scrolls и Topologika, в прошлом выпускали эксклюзивы только под +3.

Их адреса:

The Guild, 760 Tyburn Road, Erdington, Birmingham. B24 9NX.

и...

Zenobi Software, 26 Spotland Tops, Cutgate, Rochdale, Lancashire. OL12 7NX.

У обоих издателей огромный каталог игр от множества авторов. (The Guild даже продает *The Golden Cobra* от Брайна Каверса!) [С моего согласия! — Б.К.]

Сейчас Zenobi занимается переносом своего каталога из более чем 100 игр на диски формата +3, хотя во многих случаях магнитофон все еще используется для сохранения и загрузки состояний. Полноценно с дисковыми форматами работают только игры, созданные в PAW.

Компания Gilsoft, создатель PAW, адаптировала этот редактор под все системы, включая +D и +3. Владельцы кассетной версии PAW могут обновиться до версии под +D за £4.49 или до версии под +3 за £5.50.

Либо можно приобрести пакет сразу под обе системы за £20.95. Это позволит вам загружать PAW-игры с кассет и переносить их на диск (а также заменять нечитаемые шрифты, которыми грешат некоторые авторы). С Gilsoft можно связаться по адресу:

Gilsoft, 2 Park Crescent, Barry, South Glamorgan CF6 8HD.

Выбор для любителей приключений на +D широк, так что почему бы не отправить разработчикам конверт с обратным адресом (SAE), чтобы узнать свежие цены и список новинок?

— Нил Керри.
